$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose and tables of RFC 8551 sections 3.2, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.3-3.8, 3.5.3.2 and 3.10 (source .cache/rfc-8551.txt, sha256 dac39f749a08d3422bd78d4e492195067e7bc03f5fc2d0dac515f0d7ed884ae2). RFC 8551 publishes no grammar or schema for these header parameters; the tables it does print are copied in inline.verbatim.txt (I-03 to I-06, I-11, I-12). Every constraint below cites its locator and, where one exists, its requirement id rfc-8551#R-NNNN.
title: RFC 8551 S/MIME media types and their header parameters (DERIVED)
description: DERIVED. Validates one MIME entity's media type and parameters as they bear on S/MIME. INSTANCE MODEL (inferred, this library's, not the RFC's): a parsed header, not raw header text. mediaType is type/subtype lower-cased; parameters maps each Content-Type parameter name, lower-cased, to its value with any MIME quoting removed; contentDisposition, when the entity has a Content-Disposition field, holds its disposition type and parameters the same way. Because quoting is removed, the quoting requirement on the protocol parameter (R-0117) cannot be checked here; it is checked by multipart-signed-content-type.derived.abnf. TWO LEVELS. Validating against the root checks only what RFC 8551 states with MUST or as a required parameter: a failure is non-conformance. Validating against #/$defs/sendingAgentShould (anchor #should) adds the SHOULD-level sending-agent rules: a failure there is a deviation from a recommendation, to be reported as a warning, never as non-conformance. #/$defs/identifiesAsSmime (anchor #identifies) is the section 3.10 classifier and is independent of both.

mediaType.$comment: Any media type is accepted at the root; only the three below are constrained. Inferred instance model: lower-cased type/subtype.

parameters.$comment: Content-Type parameters, names lower-cased, values unquoted (inferred instance model).

contentDisposition.$comment: The Content-Disposition field [RFC2183], named in section 3.2.1 (R-0103).

smimeTypeDefined.description: The five smime-type values this specification defines (section 3.2.2, table I-04, lines 1535-1541). authEnveloped-data is the value registered by section 5.3 (I-13).
smimeTypeDefined.$comment: Not a closed set for conformance: section 3.2.2 lines 1575-1576 say a registry for additional values is defined in [RFC7114], so a value outside this list is not an error at the root. Case: the RFC prints authEnveloped-data with a capital E (lines 1541, 1661, 2420); whether matching is case-sensitive is not stated in RFC 8551 and is not decided here (open).

smimeTypeToExtension.description: The file extension each smime-type's message takes, as stated per format: enveloped-data .p7m (section 3.3, lines 1605-1607), authEnveloped-data .p7m (section 3.4, lines 1660-1662), signed-data .p7m (section 3.5.2, lines 1781-1783), compressed-data .p7z (section 3.6, lines 2029-2031), certs-only .p7c (section 3.8, lines 2106-2107). Consistent with table I-03 (section 3.2.1, lines 1488-1496).
smimeTypeToExtension.$comment: A lookup table carried as a const for harnesses to read; it validates nothing by itself.

micalgTableValue.description: The 'Value Used' column of the section 3.5.3.2 micalg table (I-05, lines 1919-1928), plus the literal "unknown" that its 'Any other' row names.
micalgTableValue.$comment: R-0119 (SHOULD be from the table). The 'Any other' row also admits values 'defined separately in the algorithm profile', and lines 1937-1938 say future values will be taken from the IANA 'Hash Function Textual Names' registry, so this enum is not closed for conformance.

micalgHistorical.description: Table values marked * in section 3.5.3.2: 'MD5 and SHA-1 are historical and no longer considered secure.' (lines 1921-1922, 1930).

micalgList.description: The micalg parameter value: one or more values separated by commas.
micalgList.$comment: Section 3.5.3.2 lines 1914-1915, R-0118: 'If multiple message digest algorithms are used, they MUST be separated by commas per [RFC1847].' Whether whitespace may surround a comma is RFC 1847's matter, not stated in RFC 8551; this pattern neither forbids nor trims it (inferred).

protocol.$comment: Section 3.5.3.2 line 1879, R-0116: 'The protocol parameter MUST be "application/pkcs7-signature".' Lower-case comparison of a media type value is the inferred instance model.

parameters.$comment: required: section 3.5.3.2 lines 1876-1877, 'The multipart/signed Content-Type has two required parameters: the protocol parameter and the micalg parameter.' (stated; not a BCP 14 keyword, no R-id). Scope (inferred): RFC 8551 constrains multipart/signed only as S/MIME uses it; a multipart/signed whose protocol is some other value is not an S/MIME message (section 3.10, I-06) and fails here only because this schema is applied to S/MIME entities. Callers that see arbitrary mail apply #/$defs/identifiesAsSmime first.
Section 5.1 (I-11, lines 2309-2312): 'Required Parameters: NONE', 'Optional Parameters: smime-type name'. Nothing is required at MUST level. Other parameters are not forbidden by RFC 8551.

pkcs7SignatureMust.$comment: Section 5.2 (I-12, lines 2365-2367): 'Required Parameters: N/A', 'Optional Parameters: N/A'. No parameter is required. The section 3.5.3.3 sample nevertheless carries name=smime.p7s (line 1980), so a name parameter is not treated as an error (inferred: the template's N/A is not read as a prohibition).

filenameShould.description: Filename rule of section 3.2.1 applied to a name or filename value.

allOf.$comment: Section 3.2.1 lines 1498-1499, R-0105: 'the filename SHOULD be limited to eight characters followed by a three-letter extension.' Reading 'eight characters' as at most eight, with no dot in the base, is inferred.
Section 3.2.1 lines 1500-1502, R-0106: 'the use of the filename base "smime" SHOULD be used to indicate that the MIME entity is associated with S/MIME.'

sendingAgentShould.description: SHOULD-level checks for what a sending agent emits. Includes the root (MUST level) by reference. Failures here are warnings.

allOf.$comment: Section 3.2.1 lines 1485-1496, R-0104, table I-03: application/pkcs7-mime takes .p7m, .p7c or .p7z.

parameters.$comment: smime-type: section 3.2 lines 1474-1477, R-0101 ('SHOULD include the optional "smime-type" parameter'). name: section 3.2.1 lines 1481-1483, R-0102. Restricting smime-type to the five defined values is a lint for this specification's own formats; registered additions (RFC 7114) will warn here.

contentDisposition.$comment: Section 3.2.1 lines 1483-1484, R-0103: 'Sending agents SHOULD also emit the optional Content-Disposition field [RFC2183] with the "filename" parameter.'

name.$comment: Section 3.5.3.1 lines 1843-1844 and table I-03: the extension for application/pkcs7-signature is .p7s. R-0104 governs name/filename for application/pkcs7-mime only (line 1481); applying it here is inferred from table I-03, which lists application/pkcs7-signature.

micalg.$comment: Section 3.5.3.2 lines 1916-1928, R-0119: each value SHOULD be from the table (#/$defs/micalgTableValue). A value defined by an algorithm profile ('Any other' row) is permitted by the source and will warn here; a harness treats that warning as informational. A receiving agent is held to R-0120 instead: it SHOULD recover gracefully from an unrecognized micalg value, so this check is NOT applied to received messages.

extensionMatchesSmimeType.description: When both smime-type and name are present on application/pkcs7-mime, the name's extension agrees with #/$defs/smimeTypeToExtension.
extensionMatchesSmimeType.$comment: These per-format statements are not BCP 14 sentences; they make concrete 'the appropriate extension' of R-0104. Filename in Content-Disposition is not cross-checked against smime-type here (inferred scope).

identifiesAsSmime.description: Section 3.10 (table I-06, lines 2149-2157): 'A message is considered an S/MIME message if it matches any of the criteria listed below.' Valid against this schema means the entity is identified as S/MIME.
identifiesAsSmime.$comment: Lines 2144-2146: the file suffix 'comes from the "name" parameter in the Content-Type header field or the "filename" parameter in the Content-Disposition header field.' Suffix matching is case-sensitive here; RFC 8551 does not say (open). Note R-0107/R-0108 (section 3.2.1): a proper implementation MUST use the media types and MUST NOT rely on the file extensions; this classifier only identifies, it does not authorize processing by extension.
